headline: Mitii AI Agent achieves 78% success rate on 500+ tasks using local Qwen3-Coder (30B)
summary: Mitii, an AI coding assistant, was benchmarked against 515 tasks, demonstrating that local LLMs can achieve top-tier performance without relying on cloud providers. Its multi-mode architecture proved highly effective, especially in complex scenarios.
details: Building an AI agent that writes safe, reliable code locally is challenging. Mitii, an AI coding assistant with a multi-mode architecture, was developed to give developers control without sending proprietary code to closed-source APIs.

Mitii underwent a rigorous manual benchmark of 515 tasks, from simple bug fixes to adversarial security injections. It was powered by qwen3-coder:30b, running entirely locally via Ollama, to test its real-world effectiveness.

The benchmark results show that local LLMs are production-ready for agents, with Mitii achieving a nearly 80% overall pass rate. This proves that high-tier AI assistance doesn't require massive cloud providers, combining Mitii's architecture with Qwen3-Coder.

Mitii's 'Ask Mode' particularly excelled, scoring an 87% win rate on Hard tasks. This mode's explicit impact analysis, detailing web searches and file modifications, makes it resilient against complex and adversarial prompts, including security attacks.

The agent also demonstrated strength in security and corner cases, performing well where it matters most. While a 78% win rate on an adversarial benchmark with a local model is significant, there's room for improvement in semantic retrieval (currently 63%) and medium-difficulty routing.

Local AI coding agent Mitii achieved a 78% success rate on over 500 tasks. It ran entirely on a local 30B parameter Qwen3-Coder model.

Mitii's 'Ask Mode' particularly excelled, scoring an 87% win rate on Hard tasks. This mode's explicit impact analysis, detailing web searches and file modifications, makes it resilient against complex and adversarial prompts, including security attacks.

The agent also demonstrated strength in security and corner cases, performing well where it matters most. While a 78% win rate on an adversarial benchmark with a local model is significant, there's room for improvement in semantic retrieval (currently 63%) and medium-difficulty routing.
